speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang
text: asked the Minister for Manpower when implementing the mandatory rest day for migrant domestic workers at the end of 2022, whether the Ministry intends to define the rest day as a full 24-hour period of uninterrupted rest.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: Different households have different arrangements with their MDWs based on their respective needs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If MOM prescribes a fixed number, it will impose rigidity on both employers and MDWs.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: What is more important is that the employer and the MDW maintain open communications on their respective needs and come to a mutual agreement on the rest day arrangement.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: If MDWs and their employers need help to reach an agreement on the rest day arrangement, they may call MOM’s MDW helpline for advice.

speaker: The Minister of State for Manpower (Ms Gan Siow Huang) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: They may also seek assistance from a neutral third party, such as their employment agencies, or consider utilising the free dispute resolution services offered by the Centre for Domestic Employees (CDE) and the Foreign Domestic Worker Association for Social Support and Training (FAST) to arrive at an amicable solution.

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Could I just ask how MOM will be monitoring and enforcing this mandatory rest day rule?

speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
text: Also, what action will be taken against employers who do not give their foreign domestic workers this mandatory rest day?
